items.followUp: State two criteria used by Whittaker in his five-kingdom classification.

rubric.why: The classification considered cellular structure and the level of body organization.
rubric.description: Identifies cell structure/type and body organization as criteria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning both criteria.

rubric.why: Nutrition, reproduction and evolutionary relationships were also considered.
rubric.description: Identifies other criteria used in the classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning at least two of these criteria.

modelAnswer: The five-kingdom classification was based on cell structure and the level of body organization.
It also considered mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.

items.followUp: What is binomial nomenclature, and who introduced it?

rubric.why: Linnaeus introduced the system of naming each species with two words.
rubric.description: States that Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the contribution.

rubric.why: Linnaeus classified organisms into the kingdoms Plantae and Animalia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both kingdoms or plants and animals.

modelAnswer: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature, in which each species is given a two-word scientific name.
He classified organisms into two kingdoms: Plantae and Animalia.

items.followUp: Name the cell organelle that contains digestive enzymes and state one function of those enzymes.

rubric.why: Lysosomes contain enzymes that digest materials inside the cell.
rubric.description: States that lysosomes carry out intracellular digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying intracellular digestion or the breakdown of materials.

rubric.why: Lysosomes can break down worn-out cell parts and foreign material.
rubric.description: Gives an example of material broken down by lysosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming worn-out organelles or foreign particles such as bacteria.

modelAnswer: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that carry out intracellular digestion.
They break down worn-out organelles and foreign particles, such as bacteria.

items.followUp: How does active transport differ from diffusion?

rubric.why: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient.
rubric.description: States the direction of movement in active transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating movement against the concentration gradient, such as from low to high concentration.

rubric.why: Energy is required for active transport.
rubric.description: States that active transport requires energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning energy or ATP.

modelAnswer: Active transport is the movement of substances across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient.
This movement requires energy, usually supplied by ATP.

items.followUp: What happens to chromosomes during anaphase of mitosis?

rubric.why: The mitotic spindle is made of spindle fibres.
rubric.description: Identifies the spindle as fibres or microtubules formed during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming spindle fibres or microtubules.

rubric.why: Spindle fibres separate and move chromosomes or chromatids toward opposite poles.
rubric.description: States the spindle's role in chromosome movement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing separation or movement toward opposite poles.

modelAnswer: The mitotic spindle is a structure of spindle fibres formed during cell division.
Its fibres attach to chromosomes and separate them, moving them toward opposite poles of the cell.

items.followUp: What happens to a plant cell when it is placed in a hypertonic solution?

rubric.why: Plasmolysis begins when a plant cell loses water in a hypertonic solution.
rubric.description: States that water leaves the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the loss or outward movement of water.

accept: cytoplasm shrinks away from cell wall
plasma membrane pulls away from cell wall
cell membrane pulls away from cell wall
rubric.why: Water loss causes the protoplast to shrink away from the cell wall.
rubric.description: Describes the shrinkage that characterizes plasmolysis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cytoplasm or protoplast shrinks away from the cell wall.

modelAnswer: Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of the protoplast when a plant cell loses water in a hypertonic solution.
As a result, the cytoplasm and cell membrane pull away from the cell wall.

items.followUp: How many daughter cells are produced by meiosis, and what is their chromosome number compared with the parent cell?

rubric.why: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half.
rubric.description: Identifies meiosis as a reduction division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the chromosome number is halved.

rubric.why: Meiosis produces four haploid daughter cells from one diploid cell.
rubric.description: States the number and chromosome condition of the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that four haploid cells are produced.

modelAnswer: Meiosis is a reduction division in which the chromosome number is halved.
It involves two successive divisions and produces four haploid daughter cells from one diploid cell.

items.followUp: Give one example of an intracellular enzyme and one example of an extracellular enzyme.

rubric.why: Intracellular enzymes act inside the cells in which they are present.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their site of action as inside the cell.

rubric.why: Extracellular enzymes are released from cells and act outside them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their site of action as outside the cell.

modelAnswer: Intracellular enzymes act inside the cells in which they are present.
Extracellular enzymes are secreted by cells and act outside the cells.
